summary: This study compared optical coherence tomography (OCT)/OCT angiography (OCTA) measures in 21 patients with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody disease (MOGAD), 21 patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and 22 controls. OCT was used to assess retinal structure, including the retinal nerve fiber layer and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer, while OCTA imaged the macula microvasculature, including the superficial vascular plexus, intermediate capillary plexus, and deep capillary plexus. The study found distinct structural and microvascular changes in MOGAD patients compared to NMOSD patients, suggesting different pathological mechanisms.
